claims.text: Medical imaging AI can propagate or amplify biases introduced in steps from model inception to deployment.
Biases introduced in medical imaging AI can result in systematic differences in the treatment of different demographic or clinical groups.
The roadmap of medical imaging AI/ML contains five main steps: data collection, data preparation and annotation, model development, model evaluation, and model deployment.
There are 29 sources of potential bias identified across the medical imaging AI/ML roadmap.

evidence.description: The authors state that medical imaging AI can propagate or amplify biases introduced in the many steps from model inception to deployment.
The paper notes that amplified biases result in a systematic difference in the treatment of different groups.

Five main steps along the roadmap of medical imaging AI/ML were identified: (1) data collection, (2) data preparation and annotation, (3) model development, (4) model evaluation, and (5) model deployment.
Within the roadmap steps, the multi-institutional panel identified 29 sources of potential bias.

methodologies.name: Multi-institutional interdisciplinary expert consensus framework
methodologies.description: A multi-institutional panel of medical physicists, AI/ML researchers, bias experts, statisticians, physicians, and regulatory scientists identified bias sources and mitigation strategies across the medical imaging AI roadmap.

limitations.text: Biases introduced in steps toward clinical deployment may impede the intended function of medical imaging AI tools and exacerbate inequities.
